 Mixed movements forecast anew for oil prices
 Oct 30, 2026
 6:52 PM GMT+8
 ADJUSTMENTS . Diesel prices are expected to reverse course next week following two consecutive weeks of increases, while gasoline prices are projected to move in the opposite direction, Jetti Petroleum president Leo Bellas said in a message to journalists on Friday (Oct. 30, 2026). Diesel prices are projected to roll back by PHP0.40 to PHP 0.60 per liter, while prices of gasoline are forecast to increase from PHP2.90 to PHP 3.20 per liter. (PNA file photo) 
 MANILA – Domestic fuel prices are once again expected to move in opposite directions in the first week of November as supply disruptions stemming from the ongoing Middle East conflict persist.
Citing price movements in Asia along with the foreign exchange path as of Thursday, Leo Bellas, Jetti President, in a message to journalists Friday, said prices of diesel will likely be slashed by PHP0.40 to PHP 0.60 per liter while prices of gasoline are forecast to increase from PHP2.90 to PHP 3.20 per liter.
This is a turnaround from the past two weeks when gasoline prices declined while diesel prices rose.
The price projections, he said, still exclude week-on-week adjustments in ocean freight and insurance."
Bellas said, "diesel and gasoline closely followed the movement of crude oil, which continues to be supported by concerns about energy supply disruptions in the Middle East as regional attacks continue and worries the US could strike Iran after next week’s US midterm elections."
He, however, "hopes for a breakthrough in the diplomatic efforts to end the eight-month-long conflict to help pare oil’s further rise."
"Furthermore, improving fuel supply prospects helped unwind diesel and gasoline gains after China issued a fourth batch of fuel export quotas for gasoline, diesel and jet fuel," he said.
An additional boost to global supply is "the easing by South Korea of its diesel export restrictions," he said.
"Russian diesel and gasoline exports also peaked amid a pause in confirmed Ukrainian refinery strikes. These factors have pressured diesel, reversing earlier gains," he added. (Joann Santiago-Villanueva/PNA)
